summary: Seiichiro Ono worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino, Kanae Tada, Daito Shimaji, and Jokan Chikazumi, later serving as professor at Tokyo (1938–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

Seiji Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University around 2005–2008 and served as an associate professor there from circa 2013 to 2022.
Seiji Nemoto works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and was a professor at the University of Tsukuba from around 2007 to 2015.
Seiji Tanaka studied under Bruno Petzold. During his career, he held positions at Asia University and at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1960–1974).
Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1976 to 1980. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University around 1999.

Seikō Hirata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. He served on the faculty at Hanazono University from around 1965 to 1998.
Sein Tin was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon (~1919–1923), Christ Church (~1923–1925), and under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927).
Seiran Ouchi was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer at Nishi Hongan-ji and as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

Seiren Matsunami specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Walther Schubring. He served as professor at Kyushu University (~1950–1967) and Rissho University (attested 1972).

Seishi Karashima worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. He studied at Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking universities under Ji Xianlin, Oskar von Hinüber, and Kenneth Norman, later becoming a professor at Soka University's IRIAB (~1998–2019).

Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923), Taisho University (1940), and Toyo University (1952, 1955).

Seitatsu Matsunami was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held an assistant post at the University of Tokyo and later served as professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).
Seitetsu Moriyama specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University in 2002 and held affiliations there in 2004 and 2013.

Seizan Yanagida worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities, learning from Shin'ichi Hisamatsu. He held professorships at Hanazono, Kyoto (~1974–1986), and Chubu (~1986–1988).
Sen Wang was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University from around 1931 to 1935 and was later a professor at Minzu University of China from circa 1952 to 1982.

Senarat Wijayasundara works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist. He succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University from around 1936 to 1937.

Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1935–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University (attested 1972).

Sengaku Mayeda worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo and Pennsylvania under Hajime Nakamura and W. Norman Brown, and held professorships at Pennsylvania (1964), Tokyo (1973–1991), and Musashino University (~1995–2001).
